        <h2>The Drifter Manifesto</h2>
        <p style="margin-bottom: 1rem; font-size: 1.1rem; line-height: 1.8; color: var(--text-dark);">
          The Drifter Manifesto is the primary theoretical reference for AffineDrift. It establishes
          the control-affine framework, introduces key concepts (ZTCF, ZVCF, Drift-Control Ratio),
          and provides the notation used throughout all AffineDrift research.
        </p>
        <div style="margin-bottom: 1.5rem; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; background: var(--bg-secondary, #f8f9fa); border-left: 3px solid var(--primary-color, #2563eb); border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--text-light, #6b7280);">
          <strong>Provenance:</strong> The control-affine form &#7715; = f(x) + g(x)u is established control theory (Isidori 1995). The drift/input decomposition, ZTCF, and DCR applied to golf biomechanics are original AffineDrift synthesis &mdash; not peer-reviewed. See <a href="../critiques/index.html">Critiques &amp; Responses</a> for documented limitations.
        </div>

        <div style="margin-bottom: 2rem; text-align: center;">

        <h3 style="margin-bottom: 1rem; color: var(--text-dark);">Contents</h3>

        <div class="article-card">
          <h3><a href="../articles/drifter-manifesto.html#sec-part1">Part 1 &mdash; State Definition and Affine Derivation</a></h3>
          <p>Establishes the multibody coordinates, derives the control-affine structure, and sets the notation used throughout. Introduces the abstract and the core question: how much of swing motion is "inevitable" versus "chosen"?</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-card">
          <h3><a href="../articles/drifter-manifesto.html#sec-part2">Part 2 &mdash; Drift/Input Decomposition, ZTCF, and ZVCF</a></h3>
          <p>Formalizes how to separate passive dynamics from deliberate torque using the Zero Torque Counterfactual (ZTCF) and Zero Velocity Counterfactual (ZVCF).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-card">
          <h3><a href="../articles/drifter-manifesto.html#sec-part3">Part 3 &mdash; Drift Invariance and Force Taxonomy</a></h3>
          <p>Explores drift invariance properties, introduces a complete force taxonomy, and discusses limitations of the affine assumption.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-card">
          <h3><a href="../articles/drifter-manifesto.html#sec-part4">Part 4 &mdash; Modal Approximation, Wrenches, and Pendulum Dynamics</a></h3>
          <p>Collects detailed mathematical derivations, modal approximations of the flexible shaft, and pendulum model examples that support the main theory.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-card">
          <h3><a href="../articles/drifter-manifesto.html#sec-part5">Part 5 &mdash; Numerical Consistency Check (Planar Model)</a></h3>
          <p>Documents the numerical implementation, Simulink validation, and supporting technical notes for the planar golf swing model.</p>
        </div>
